# Disagreement Log — Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 14

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Chapter:** POX 14 — Joseph's dilemma; the angelic dream; Joseph's response

---

## Disagreements

**1. 14:1 — "I will be found fighting against the law"**
- EMET: "I will be found fighting against the law of the Lord"
- LOGOS: "I will be found to have acted against the law of the Lord"
- PNEUMA: "I'm breaking God's law"
- Note: Greek *heurethēsomai machomenos tō nomō Kyriou* = "I will be found fighting against the law of the Lord." EMET preserves the vivid military image "fighting against." PNEUMA drops this entirely.

**2. 14:1 — "reveal her" vs. "expose her"**
- EMET: "reveal her to the children of Israel"
- LOGOS: "expose her to the children of Israel"
- PNEUMA: "report her to the people"
- Note: Greek *apokalysō* = "reveal/uncover/expose." All are acceptable; LOGOS's "expose" captures the public-shaming sense best.

**3. 14:1 — "from an angel"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "from an angel"
- PNEUMA: "from an angel"
- Note: Joseph fears the child may have a supernatural father. The text here does NOT say "Holy Spirit" — Joseph doesn't know that yet. This is resolved in 14:2. All three agents preserve this correctly.

**4. 14:1 — "put her away from me secretly" vs. "divorce her quietly"**
- EMET: "I will put her away from me secretly"
- LOGOS: "I will divorce her quietly"
- PNEUMA: "I'll just quietly let her go"
- Note: Greek *apolysai autēn lathraios* = "to release/dismiss her secretly." LOGOS uses "divorce" which is correct legally; EMET's "put away" is the older English equivalent (Matt 1:19). PNEUMA's "let her go" is too casual.

**5. 14:2 — Angel's address**
- EMET: "Do not fear because of this child" (no name for Joseph)
- LOGOS: "Joseph, do not be afraid on account of this child"
- PNEUMA: "Joseph, don't be afraid because of this child"
- Note: LOGOS/PNEUMA add "Joseph" as vocative — may be present in some MSS; absent in others including P.Bodmer V.

**6. 14:3 — "who had given this grace to him"**
- EMET: "who had given this grace to him"
- LOGOS: "who had shown him this grace"
- PNEUMA: "for giving him this revelation"
- Note: Greek *tēn charin tautēn* = "this grace/favor." PNEUMA's "revelation" (*apokalypsis*) is an interpretive substitution; the Greek word is *charis*.

**7. 14:3 — "kept her safe" vs. "kept watch over her"**
- EMET/PNEUMA: "kept her safe"
- LOGOS: "kept watch over her"
- Note: Greek *ephylaxen autēn* = "guarded/kept her." Both renderings capture the sense; LOGOS slightly emphasizes vigilance, EMET emphasizes safety.
